latestCommit.description:
## Scope

Step 3 of the report-v1 migration. Site phase C (#20, a190fb7) switched
the shared site (mitsevox/mitsevox.github.io) to importing nflstreet2's
`report-v1` package and archived the legacy reader.

- **`.github/workflows/baseline.yml`:** removes the Pages job,
`upload-pages-artifact`, and the published-history prepare/preserve
steps. It keeps the `report-v1` package and the decomp.dev
`GN7E69_report` upload.
- **`tools/restore_history.py`** (rewritten): main restores history by
merging two authenticated sources.
- The first is the `report-v1` package of the newest successful `main`
run (push or workflow_dispatch, among the last 50) on this revision's
history, chosen via `publication.report_v1_artifact`. Runs that are off
this history, or that have no usable package, are skipped. The checks
are:
    - the artifact digest and size limit
    - that the entries are regular files
    - that the manifest revision equals the run head
- the timeline sha256, with the timeline read from the path the manifest
names
- The second is the site's accepted package on `report-data`. It is
checked against `data/reports.lock.json`: the manifest sha256 and
revision must equal the lock, and the revision must be an ancestor.
- Restore fails if the merged history would change any row the site
accepted, because the site rejects such imports. It also fails if
neither source is available, so it never resets history.
- **`tools/report_v1.py`:** adds `provenance_of`, the inverse of
`source()`, and `history_feed`, which turns a timeline-v1 back into the
activity feed.
- **Removed:** `config/GN7E69/history-recovery.json` and its docs. The
docs are updated, and the README links to `/games/nflstreet2/`.

**Site policy:** the `baseline.yml` blob changes from `98a97409…` to
`f209bfa23df04f7da077f4ca93154da6fe8dddce`. Site #21 (f010fc0) approves
it.

After merge, the owner can disable GitHub Pages in the repo settings.

## Evidence and validation

- `LIVE_RECEIPTS=false python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 339 OK. A
clean checkout skips 22 tests that need CI tools. The RestoreTests
cover:
  - the timeline↔feed round trip
  - merging the main package with the site store
  - skipped runs
  - restoring from the store alone, in both legacy and v1 formats
  - no source available
- a tampered digest, wrong revision, tampered store manifest, or
non-ancestor store
  - a main package changing an accepted row (provenance or built_at)
  - package entries following the manifest
- Live: `python3 tools/restore_history.py --revision origin/main`
(855854d8) authenticated main run 40258381140 (artifact 12623383861) and
the site store snapshot. It restored 161 rows, identical to the store.
Both reviewers replayed the site's own `check_update` on the
round-tripped timeline plus a next row, and it was accepted.

## Review

- Reviewed revision: 270b5277b955129aa3375a04ed81a21fad890564
- Independent accuracy pass: [FAIL at
10661de](https://github.com/mitsevox/nflstreet2/pull/1134#issuecomment-6407247538),
then [delta PASS at
270b527](https://github.com/mitsevox/nflstreet2/pull/1134#issuecomment-6407295636)
- Fresh hostile pass and recheck: [FIX at
10661de](https://github.com/mitsevox/nflstreet2/pull/1134#issuecomment-6407233307),
then [delta SHIP at
270b527](https://github.com/mitsevox/nflstreet2/pull/1134#issuecomment-6407285596)

Optional follow-up (hostile note): the committed seed is merged later,
at export and promote, without the store-row check. A future edit to
`history.json` that altered an accepted row would be rejected by the
site rather than reset anything.
